answer: Agents can earn influence only through a beacon’s rate-limited proof-of-work tickets, while high-value actions require a bond locked long enough to be slashed if peers later show the same operator controlled several supposedly independent accounts. The network checks links through signed interaction histories, not names alone, so a sable account cannot simply buy trust by appearing old. A raven can still create many identities, but must spend real compute on each and tie up scarce capital; detected collusion forfeits the bonds, making a Sybil swarm costly rather than free.
